newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets up site for natural gas distribution.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets up site for natural gas distribution.

text.p: Mexico designated the metropolitan area surrounding Saltillo, Coahuila state, as a bidding site for natural gas distribution rights, Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission said in Thursday's official government gazette.
The southeast region of the U.S-Mexico border state is one of several zones being established by the Mexican government for private bidding in natural gas distribution.

"Saltillo-Ramos Arizpe-Arteaga is an important center of state services, with influence throughout the state and 1,189 manufacturing establishments and 6,076 dedicated to trade ... that would benefit from the use of a more competitive fuel such as natural gas," the commission said.
Estimated daily consumption for the area is "seven billion kilocalories per day," the commission said.
Companies that have already expressed interest in distributing the region's natural gas include Repsol Mexico, which also is expected to bid for the nearby Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas state concession.

The biddings are part of the Mexican government's strategy to boost the use of natural gas, which is cleaner than other currently used fuels. Many Mexican cities do not currently have a widespread natural gas distribution network.

Mexico granted the distribution concession in Mexicali, Baja California state to Mexican-American consortium Distribuidora de Gas Natural de Mexicali (DGN), which comprises Mexican firm Proxima and U.S. firms Pacific Enterprises and Enova-San Diego Gas and Electric.
Bids for natural gas distribution rights in the Chihuahua state zone, the second to be doled out, will be accepted through Jan. 23, 1997 with a decision due by March 20, 1997.
The government has also defined the towns of Hermosillo, Guaymas and Empalme in Sonora state as a single zone for natural gas distribution purposes.
